message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations that drivers should know: | Topic | Key Points | Practical Tips | |-------|------------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must still drive at a safe speed for conditions. | • Always obey posted signs; if none, use common sense and adjust for weather, traffic, and road conditions. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Laws** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | • Check that all passengers are buckled before you start driving. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Use a Bluetooth headset or voice‑control features. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • Never drive after drinking; use rideshare or a designated driver. | | **Traffic Signal & Stop‑Sign Rules** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs, even if no one is approaching.
• Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks. | • Practice “stop‑and‑look” before proceeding. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right.
• In school zones, yield to school buses stopping to pick up or drop off children. | • Slow down in school zones and watch for stopped buses. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | • Keep a safe following distance (at least 2–3 seconds). | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 15 mph during school hours (usually 7 a.m.–9 p.m.) in designated zones. | • Pay attention to flashing signs and reduce speed accordingly. | | **High‑way Lane‑Use** | • Use the right lane for normal traffic; use the left lane for passing only.
• Do not drive in the left lane on a freeway unless passing. | • Stay in the right lane unless overtaking. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, stop signs, or crosswalks.
• No parking on sidewalks unless permitted. | • Read parking signs carefully; avoid fines. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• All vehicles must have a valid registration sticker.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | • Check your registration sticker and tire tread before trips. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. | • Stay calm and let the emergency vehicle pass. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • If your vehicle is towed, you may be liable for towing fees.
• Texas law requires towing companies to provide a written estimate. | • Keep receipts and document any disputes. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | • Maintain proof of insurance in your vehicle. | | **Traffic School** | • Eligible for a traffic‑school waiver if you have a clean record and meet other criteria. | • Check eligibility and apply before receiving a ticket. | ### Quick Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** | Official traffic rules, maps, and updates. | | **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** | Licensing, registration, and insurance info. | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement and safety tips. | | **Texas Traffic Law Center** | Legal advice and case law. | ### Tips for Staying Safe & Legal 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they’re there for safety. 2. **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – brakes, lights, tires, and mirrors. 3. **Avoid distractions** – put your phone away, focus on the road. 4. **Know your limits** – if you’re tired, drunk, or ill, don’t drive. 5. **Stay informed** – traffic laws can change; keep up with official updates. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or have a particular scenario in mind, let me know!
